items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: For instance like if I’m playing with the Rolling Stones I’m improvising every night on “Miss You” this famous song of theirs. But that solo is when Mick is out front in front of 50,000 people

ctx.x: Yes. I mean well for instance last night it was more open-ended and I didn’t have to limit, as you said, limit myself. I could do one, two, three or four or five. Like there was a period where that accordion player, Al, came up and sat in right. So now we’re incorporating a guy who does polka music with the accordion, because Ron Oswanski also is an amazing accordion player and can do the polkas, he grew up in a Polish household and he played all that stuff. But he also can improvise and play jazz, he’s…

figure out what — so then we did this Ukrainian polka because of the Ukrainian situation. But Ron and I had done, I had to produce an album for Ron and we did that song on his record but we did it kind of like as a North African kind of vibe combined with this polka. So we tried to do that last night with Al but then on that I didn’t really improvise. I kind of let Al — which I played the melody with him and then just a little tiny solo, Ron would play a little solo, so just it was more about how do we feature,…
Yeah. That’s an astute player required for that kind of thing I think. And your solos, like that particular solo that’s probably like a one chord vamp?
